restaurant_name: Dr. Wirath Medical Clinic | คลินิกเวชกรรมน.พ.วิรัตน์
text:
Honestly, I would have paid even more!

My child apparently got salmonella/food poisoning from a street food waffle.

After seven hours of vomiting every 20 minutes during the night, I decided to ask the hotel for help.

The doctor and his assistant arrived within half an hour.

They started an IV drip on my child. The infusion lasted three hours (!).

The doctors explained everything to me and stayed in contact via WhatsApp.

We also received some medication and electrolytes.

The fever (39.5°C/103.5°F) went down.

The vomiting stopped immediately. The diarrhea persisted, but the doctors explained this to me.

Yes, 18,000 baht isn't cheap, but it was worth every single euro!

My child was unresponsive, and in my opinion, Dr. Wirath and his team did the best they could for my child.

I hope it stays that way!

text:
In 2019, I visited Dr. Wirath at his villa to treat a friend's child. I found him very professional and kind, and I admired him greatly.

I recently developed a fever and remembered this clinic, so I decided to come for an injection. Today's experience was quite unpleasant: I had already filled out my guest information at the front desk, but when I saw the doctor, she asked where I lived and what I did for work. I didn't understand if she wanted a general area or a specific address, and it was the first time I'd been asked such detailed questions at a hospital. So I hesitated, intending to show her my work ID on my phone. Before I could even produce it, she impatiently scolded me: "Don't you even know where you live?! Don't you know what you do for a living?"

Me: "Excuse me?" I immediately turned and left, deciding it was pointless to look.
